records.summary: 200 Capp St operated as a bar (DBA Uptown) with a Type 48 full-bar license until February 21, 2024, when the license was surrendered—the same day as this report. The space sits in the Mission Street NCT district where a bar is a conditional use, and inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which requires any new bar to use a Type 48 license transferred from another bar already located within the district. The block is densely developed with food and drink businesses: 21 registered businesses within 500 feet and four active ABC on-sale licenses. The records contain no dated Planning Commission decisions for comparable bar or nightlife uses within 1,000 feet in the last ten years, so no approval rate can be shown.

comparables.why_comparable: This is an agency referral for the exact same address (200 Capp St) in 2019, approving continuation of the existing bar use (DBA Uptown) with a Type 48 license in the NCT-MISSION district and Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved continuation of the bar use at this location but explicitly stated no intensification or expansion would be allowed in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD without a conditional use authorization. This is an agency referral, not a Commission hearing, so it shows administrative approval but not full discretionary review.

comparables.why_comparable: Earlier agency referral at the same address (200 Capp St) in 2015 approving an ownership transfer of the Type 48 license for the existing bar use (DBA Uptown) per Planning Code Section 249.60(c) governing the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved a Type 48 ownership transfer at this exact location under the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD rules. Both this and the 2019 referral were continuations of an existing bar, not establishment of a new bar use, which is the critical distinction in the Special Use District.

comparables.why_comparable: Agency referral 195 meters away at 2901 16th St approving a Type 48 license for a restaurant/bar use. The record explicitly states the license was transferred from within the Mission Alcohol Restrict SUD (from 2950 16th Street City Club), demonstrating compliance with the district's transfer requirement.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved a Type 48 bar use in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD by confirming the license was transferred from another location already within the district, as required by Planning Code Section 249.60(c). This shows the pathway for establishing bar use in the SUD: transfer from within the district.

comparables.why_comparable: Second agency referral for the same 2901 16th St project (Board of Supervisors/Public Convenience or Necessity referral), 195 meters away, also noting the Type 48 license transfer from within the Mission Alcohol Restrict SUD and that it was not treated as a change of use under Planning Code Section 843.45.
comparables.key_takeaway: The dual referrals show both Planning and ABC coordination was required. The finding that restaurant-to-bar was not a 'change of use' under Section 843.45 when the license came from within the district suggests flexibility when the SUD transfer requirement is met.

comparables.why_comparable: Conditional Use Authorization 192 meters away at 2022 Mission St in NCT-MISSION district, approved in 2021 for a restaurant with place of entertainment use allowing operation until 2:00 a.m. This is a Commission hearing decision, not an agency referral.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning Commission approved entertainment use with 2 a.m. closing in the same NCT-MISSION corridor. Standard conditions included noise control, soundproofing, community liaison, and notices posted at entrances. Approval took 8 months from filing to decision, demonstrating the timeline for a conditional use hearing.

comparables.why_comparable: Conditional Use Authorization 178 meters away at 2034 Mission St in NCT-MISSION for a limited restaurant upgrading to full restaurant to serve beer and wine, approved with 10 p.m. closing. Commission hearing decision approved in 6 months.
comparables.key_takeaway: Commission approved alcohol service expansion in the NCT-MISSION corridor but imposed a 10 p.m. closing condition for a beer-and-wine restaurant. The restrictive hours suggest concern about late-night impacts in this neighborhood, even for lower-intensity alcohol uses.

comparables.why_comparable: Conditional Use Authorization 222 meters away at 2214 Mission St in NCT-MISSION for outdoor dining, approved September 2023 with 10 p.m. outdoor closing. Commission decision showing recent approval patterns in the immediate area.
comparables.key_takeaway: Recent Commission approval on the Mission corridor imposed 10 p.m. closing for outdoor activity and required notices posted at bars and entertainment venues. This mirrors the pattern from other nearby approvals: the Commission is approving uses but managing impacts through hours restrictions and patron behavior conditions.

comparables.why_comparable: Agency referral 261 meters away at 647 Valencia St (NCT-VALENCIA district) approving continuation of existing bar use with Type 48 license. Multiple approvals at this location show a longstanding bar use in the neighboring Valencia corridor.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning routinely approved continuation of the existing bar use at 647 Valencia over many years. This is an agency referral for continuation, not establishment, but it shows Planning's administrative approval of Type 48 bars when the use is already established.

patterns.pattern: Agency referrals for continuation or ownership transfer of existing bar uses in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD were administratively approved when no intensification occurred. New or expanded bar uses require conditional use authorization.

Type 48 licenses for new bar establishments in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District were approved only when the license was transferred from another bar already located within the district, per Planning Code Section 249.60(c).

Conditional Use Authorizations for eating, drinking, and entertainment uses on the Mission Street corridor in NCT-MISSION were approved with conditions including community liaison, soundproofing/noise control, and notices posted urging patrons to leave quietly.

Recent conditional use approvals in the NCT-MISSION district imposed closing hours between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m., with 10 p.m. closings for outdoor areas and lower-intensity uses, suggesting the Commission manages late-night impacts through hour restrictions.

No conditional use denials or withdrawals for bar or nightlife uses appear in the records within 1,000 feet of 200 Capp St in the past ten years, though the records note zero dated Commission decisions for comparable bar uses in that radius.

findings.text: The address sits in the Mission Street NCT district, where a bar on the first story is a conditional use under Planning Code Section 754, in force from January 14, 2024.

The Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District treats a new or relocated bar as a conditional use and requires the bar to use a liquor license transferred from another bar located inside the district, per Planning Code Section 249.60(b)(2)(C).

NCT-MISSION Table 754 Note 7 caps eating and drinking uses (Restaurants, Limited Restaurants and Bars) in the district at 179 total, and a new one is not permitted if it would take the total above that; the records do not show how many exist.

At 2901 16th St, 195 meters away in the UMU district, Planning approved a Type 48 bar use in 2017 after confirming the license was transferred from 2950 16th Street City Club, already within the Mission Alcohol Restrict SUD.

The Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District requires all liquor establishments to comply with Planning Code Section 202.2 operating conditions, and new or relocated ones must provide outside lighting, keep window signage to 33% and maintain 50% clear glazing on street-facing facades, per Section 249.60(d).

approvals.summary: The description does not state what alcohol will be served (beer and wine, or spirits) or how the license will be obtained (new application or transfer), so the rules cannot determine which ABC license type applies or whether it is available; insufficient information.

findings.text: A bar use requires either an ABC Type 42 (beer and wine bar) or Type 48 (full-liquor bar) license; the concept description states alcohol will be served but does not specify the type.
The Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District requires a new bar to use a Type 48 license transferred from another bar already within the district, not a new license issued by ABC.

The Type 48 license at 200 Capp St (ABC #559557) was surrendered on February 21, 2024, the same day as this report, ending the bar use (DBA Uptown) that operated at this address from at least 2015 through early 2024.
ABC records show 44 active on-sale licenses within 1,000 feet of the address, including four within 500 feet, indicating the census tract may be an undue-concentration area for ABC purposes.

approvals.summary: A bar serving drinks without food requires a health permit to operate, issued after inspection and plan review without a discretionary hearing; allowed.

findings.text: A bar serving drinks to the public requires a San Francisco Department of Public Health permit to operate, issued after inspection under the California Retail Food Code and San Francisco Health Code Article 8.

The health permit application is referred to Planning for a zoning review; at 200 Capp St in 2019, Planning approved a health permit referral for continuation of the existing bar use (DBA Uptown) with Type 48 license.

expected_conditions.condition: The Type 48 liquor license must be transferred from another bar located within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code Section 249.60(b)(2)(C) requires a new bar in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD to use a license transferred from another bar inside the district. Two 2017 referrals at 2901 16th St confirmed the license came from 2950 16th Street City Club within the district before approval.

expected_conditions.condition: Comply with Planning Code Section 202.2 operating conditions: maintain a community liaison, post a telephone number, and implement a good-neighbor policy including soundproofing and litter control.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code Section 249.60(d) requires all liquor establishments in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD to comply with Section 202.2. Recent CUA approvals at 2022 Mission St and 2214 Mission St imposed community liaison and patron behavior notices as conditions.

expected_conditions.condition: Provide outside lighting, keep window signage to 33% of window area, and maintain 50% clear glazing on street-facing facades.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code Section 249.60(d) imposes these requirements on new, relocated, or expanded liquor establishments in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District.

expected_conditions.condition: Soundproofing and noise control measures so that incidental noise is not audible beyond the premises and fixed-source equipment noise does not exceed the decibel levels in the Noise Control Ordinance.
expected_conditions.basis: Recent CUA approvals at 2022 Mission St (2020-011615CUA) and 2034 Mission St (2021-006276CUA) and 2214 Mission St (2023-001895CUA) all imposed soundproofing and noise control conditions on eating and drinking uses in the NCT-MISSION corridor.

expected_conditions.condition: Post well-lit notices at all entrances and exits urging patrons to leave the establishment and neighborhood quietly and not to litter or block driveways.
expected_conditions.basis: CUA approvals at 2022 Mission St (2020-011615CUA) and 2214 Mission St (2023-001895CUA) in NCT-MISSION imposed this condition on bars and entertainment venues.

expected_conditions.condition: Hours of operation limited to between 6 a.m. or 8 a.m. and 10 p.m. or 2 a.m., depending on the concept and neighborhood context.

The Commission manages late-night impacts through hour restrictions.

filing_playbook.action: Request a written answer from San Francisco Planning confirming the current count of eating and drinking uses in NCT-MISSION against the 179-unit cap.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a Letter of Determination request or call the zoning information desk at Planning and ask for the count of Restaurants, Limited Restaurants, and Bars in the Mission Street NCT district as of today, against the 179-unit cap in Planning Code Section 754 Table 754 Note 7, in effect from January 14, 2024. Ask whether a new bar at 200 Capp St would exceed the cap. If the cap is already reached, ask whether the prior bar use at the address (DBA Uptown, operated until February 21, 2024) counts toward the cap and whether reopening the bar use would be treated as a new use or a continuation.

filing_playbook.action: Engage a liquor license broker to identify and secure a Type 48 license from another bar located within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District that is willing to transfer.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Tell the broker the license must come from a bar (Type 48 holder) currently located within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District boundaries, as required by Planning Code Section 249.60(b)(2)(C). Confirm the source location and that the seller has no outstanding ABC violations. Do not close on the license purchase until Planning has issued the Conditional Use Authorization, because the CUA is required before ABC will approve the transfer. Make the lease contingent on obtaining both the CUA and the license transfer approval.

filing_playbook.action: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning for a bar use at 200 Capp St, referencing the Type 48 license transfer from within the Mission SUD.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the bar will use a Type 48 license transferred from [source address within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD]. Commit to all Planning Code Section 202.2 operating conditions: appoint a community liaison, post a contact telephone number, implement a good-neighbor policy including soundproofing and litter control within a one-block radius. Commit to the Section 249.60(d) facade and lighting requirements: provide outside lighting, limit window signage to 33% of window area, and maintain 50% clear glazing on street-facing facades. Propose operating hours (state the proposed closing time; expect the Commission may condition it). Describe the concept as a neighborhood bar with recorded music, no food service, and no live entertainment or dancing. Include a sound study if the space shares walls or floors with residential units.

filing_playbook.action: After the Planning Commission approves the CUA, file the Type 48 license transfer application with ABC, and submit the CUA approval as part of the ABC application.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: ABC will refer the application to Planning and to the Police Department ABC Liaison Unit. Planning will issue a referral response confirming the CUA has been granted. The Police Department will review the operator's background and the location. Budget 90 to 180 days from filing to ABC issuing the transferred license, plus time for public posting and any protests. Do not open or serve alcohol until ABC issues the license.

filing_playbook.action: File a building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements and exterior signage, routing it to Planning for zoning review under Planning Code Section 175.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit plans showing the bar layout, finishes, any structural or mechanical work, and the occupant load calculation. Attach the approved CUA. If the occupant load is 50 or more, the space is Assembly Group A-2 and the permit must address accessibility, exits, and fire-safety systems for that group. If fewer than 50, it is Group B. Identify the existing occupancy group and whether a change of occupancy is triggered; if so, the permit must bring the space into full code compliance for the new group. Route the sign permit through Planning for compliance with Article 6 sign controls.

filing_playbook.action: After the building permit is issued and construction is complete, schedule the final DBI inspection and apply for the health permit to operate from San Francisco Department of Public Health.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The health permit application will be referred to Planning, which will confirm the CUA and building permit are in place. DPH will inspect to confirm the bar meets health code requirements for a beverage service facility: handwashing sinks, janitorial facilities, and proper storage. The permit is issued after the inspection passes. All staff who handle drinks or ice must obtain California Food Handler Cards within 30 days of hire, and at least one owner or manager must hold a Certified Food Protection Manager certificate if any food is served.

timeline_cost.notes: The day and cost ranges cover the Conditional Use Authorization (120 to 300 days, $3,100 to $15,000 per the catalog) from filing to Commission approval, which is the critical path. These are times and costs to approval for the CUA. ABC license transfer (90 to 180 days, cost depends on the purchase price of the license from the seller, typically $100,000 to $450,000 in San Francisco) and the building permit (14 to 120 days, $800 to $15,000) run in parallel or follow the CUA. The CUA timeline depends on pre-application meetings, environmental review, hearing scheduling, and any appeals; the catalog estimates 120 to 300 days. The building permit depends on the scope of tenant improvements and plan completeness. Government fees for the CUA, building permit, business registration, sign permit, and health permit total roughly $4,000 to $17,000; the Type 48 license purchase from another bar is the largest cost but is paid to a private seller, not a government agency, so it is not included in the cost range shown here. If the count of eating and drinking uses in NCT-MISSION is already at or above the 179-unit cap, the CUA may not be grantable, in which case no time or cost to approval can be given until Planning confirms the count.
